subject: SIG evidence: PDF proof-of-origin & packaging plan for portal upload
messages:
From: Megan Olson <megan.olson@datacove.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@datacove.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG packaging question — PDF signatures / proof-of-origin

Hi Priyom,

Quick question as we prepare the procurement packet for our security review: our portal (OneTrust) enforces a "proof-of-origin" check on uploaded PDFs and flags any files where embedded fonts or incremental updates alter the checksum. Several vendors in the past have had the wrong incrementally-saved PDFs rejected.

For the SIG you sent over, can you confirm: 1) whether the exported PDF contains any digital signatures or incremental save history, 2) whether you can provide a separate manifest CSV mapping each evidence PDF to the control it supports, and 3) if you can provide a short note on canonicalization (PDF/A vs normal PDF) so our upload team knows what to expect.

We need this by EOD Tuesday to stay on our procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Megan
Megan Olson
Procurement Manager, Datacove
megan.olson@datacove.com

[Attachment: none]

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Megan Olson <megan.olson@datacove.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG packaging question — PDF signatures / proof-of-origin

Hi Megan,

Thanks for flagging this — appreciate the heads up on OneTrust's checksum checks. Short answers first:
- Export: the attached SIG_Responses_2026-12-14.pdf is a fresh flattened export (no incremental save history), produced from our evidence authoring tool with "linearize for web" disabled.
- Digital signatures: we do not apply PAdES/PKCS#7 digital signatures to evidence PDFs; the signatures you see in some vendor packets are often audit-signing or DocuSign wrappers — we keep those separate.
- Manifest: attached is evidence-manifest-DCV-987654.csv mapping file names to the SIG question IDs and the originating evidence source.
- Canonicalization: we can provide a PDF/A-2b export if you need archival canonicalization, but note that PDF/A may change fonts/embedding behavior. For OneTrust checksum stability we recommend delivering the flattened PDF plus the manifest; if the portal requires PDF/A we can generate that as a second artifact.

I have cc'd Lauren (policy ops) and Karthik (procurement playbooks) to confirm upload best practices. If EOD Tuesday is the cutoff, we can deliver the flattened PDFs and manifest by tomorrow close of business.

Attached: SIG_Responses_2026-12-14.pdf (PDF, ~1.2MB); evidence-manifest-DCV-987654.csv (CSV)

Best,
Priyom Das
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
[Attachment: SIG_Responses_2026-12-14.pdf, evidence-manifest-DCV-987654.csv]

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG packaging question — internal notes

Quick internal notes for the upload bundle (short checklist):
- Use flattened, non-incremental PDF export from our evidence repo (we already have that).
- Include an "original-hash" column in the manifest (SHA256 of the PDF bytes) so the portal can accept evidence even if it re-serializes the file.
- If Datacove wants PDF/A we should add it as "PDF_A_version" column with the PDF/A filename; keep both versions in the bundle.
- For OneTrust: prefer a single zip with consistent filenames and the manifest at the root. Avoid filenames with spaces or non-ASCII.
- Add a small README-Upload.txt that explains the conventions (fields in manifest, timestamp format).

I'll draft README-Upload and run a quick checksum pass. Karthik — if you have procurement-specific naming (deal prefix), paste it here and I'll fold it in.

—Lauren

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Megan Olson <megan.olson@datacove.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, procurement@datacove.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: SIG packaging question — PDF proof-of-origin & packaging plan for portal upload

Hi Megan — following up with the plan and attachments. Apologies for the slightly long note; wanted to be explicit about steps so your upload team has everything they need.

Plan summary (what you'll receive):
1) SIG_Responses_2026-12-14.pdf — flattened export (no incremental updates). We validated that the PDF contains no embedded digital signatures and used a single-pass generator to avoid incremental save metadata.
2) evidence-manifest-DCV-987654.csv — columns: filename, SIG_question_id, control_id, original_sha256, pdf_a_available (yes/no), pdf_a_filename
3) README-Upload.txt — short upload instructions, filename conventions, timestamp format (ISO 8601), and recommended zip structure.
4) Optional: we can produce PDF/A-2b versions on request and include pdf_a_filename links in the manifest.

Upload instructions for OneTrust (practical tips):
- Create a single zip named RDW-DCV-DL987654-evidence.zip.
- Place manifest and README at the zip root so the portal imports them first.
- If OneTrust rejects an upload due to a checksum mismatch, ask the portal team to compare the manifest original_sha256 with the stored file. We can re-generate a canonical checksum from our side on request.

We are happy to:
- Upload the zip to your OneTrust request if you can add redwood.inference@onetrust (or provide an upload token), OR
- Provide the zip via a time-limited S3 link (I can send once you confirm the recipient list).

Related links: your portal request: https://onetrust.datacove.com/portal/requests/REQ-8921; internal deal record: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/987654

Attached are the flattened PDF and the manifest used to assemble the bundle. Per your timeline, this should hit your team before EOD Tuesday — please confirm whether you want the PDF/A variants as well.

Thanks,
Priyom
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
[Attachment: SIG_Responses_2026-12-14.pdf, evidence-manifest-DCV-987654.csv]
